The tamed Magpie is very hardy, and will live for a numberof years, if he has his liberty, without forsaking those whoare kind to him: but a Magpie in a cage is a poor-lookingthing, bedraggled and dirty, and when hopping about withhis wing cut, he presents a more forlorn appearance still.Moral: keep silver spoons and jewellery out of his reach. CHAPTER XXI. THE JACKDAW. IOXCE had a Jackdaw, but only for a very short time,and, indeed, there is some doubt whether he was reallymine at all, so I cannot say a great deal about the bird,except that it is even more easily and more perfectly tamedthan the Magpie; though far from being as handsome a bird,it is a general favourite with schoolboys, learning to say afew words, and to come and go at command.
